title: Śrī Govinda Kuṇḍa Māhātmya
author: Sanskrit verses from Śrī Girirāj-khaṇḍam, Śrī Garga-saṁhitā.
subtitle: The Glories of Śrī Govinda Kuṇḍa

text: atha govardhane ramye surabhir gauḥ samudra-jā
tatra snātvā naraḥ sākṣād govinda-padam āpnuyāt
translation: *Śrīla Bhakti Sundar Govinda Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj’s corresponding Bengali composition:*
Surabhī, the divine cow who appeared from churning the milk ocean, lovingly bathed Vrajendra Nandan Kṛṣṇa with her own milk.

text: sei dugdhe pūrṇa kuṇḍa ‘śrī govinda’ nāma
translation: The pond filled with that milk, ‘Śrī Govinda Kuṇḍa’, graces beautiful Govardhan with exquisite beauty.

The transcendental water of this kuṇḍa can banish even the greatest sins. The threefold miseries – ādhyātmik, ādhidaivik, and ādhibhautik – and all fears of this material world are destroyed by bathing in or drinking this water.
Sometimes, by great fortune, someone will get to taste the water of Govinda Kuṇḍa as that milk, and, attaining a transcendentally joyful form, go to Kṛṣṇaloka.

text: śrī kṛṣṇa-mānase yebā kare hethā snāna
translation: Anyone who bathes in Śrī Govinda Kuṇḍa desiring to serve Kṛṣṇa, attains the divine service of Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa in Gupta Govardhan (hidden Govardhan).
